chapter.name: Symmetrical Designs
chapter.names_note: Vary names across regions, religions and genders; use {{NAME_n}} tokens (n up to 10, one character = one token) and list them in name_slots.json; Keeko raises the wrong idea or a real-life link at the end of a concept video.

source: Prem and Manu's Birthday Cutouts
Prem wants to cut out the letter M from a folded paper. Whic

items.question: Prem wants to cut out the letter M from a folded paper. Which fold should Prem use, and how much of the M must be drawn?
steps: Look at the M. The left side and the right side match, so the M has a vertical line of symmetry.
Fold the paper in half along the vertical line.
Draw half of the M, which is 1/2 of the letter, along the fold.
Cut along the outline and open the paper: the full M appears.
Check: the top and the bottom of the M do not match, so it has no horizontal line. One fold is all that works, and a quarter is not enough.
items.answer: Fold the paper in half along the vertical line and draw 1/2 of the M

videos.answer: Fold the paper in half along the vertical line and draw 1/2 of the M

source: Which lines of symmetry do the letters B, W and H have?

items.question: Which lines of symmetry do the letters B, W and H have?
steps: B: fold along a vertical line. The left side is straight and the right side has two bumps, so the halves do not match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top bump lands on the bottom bump, so the halves match. B has a horizontal line only.
W: fold along a vertical line. The left half lands on the right half, so they match. Fold along a horizontal line. The top and the bottom do not match. W has a vertical line only.
H: fold along a vertical line and the halves match. Fold along a horizontal line and the halves match. H has both lines.
Check: only H has two lines, so only H needs a quarter fold.
items.answer: B: horizontal line only. W: vertical line only. H: both lines

videos.answer: B: horizontal line only. W: vertical line only. H: both lines

source: Alphabet Cutout: which letters can be cut out

items.question: Which of the following alphabet cutouts can be made by just drawing half (1/2) or quarter (1/4) of the letter? You can do it by drawing lines of symmetry on the letters. The letters are E, N, X, T, K, V and O.
steps: A letter can be cut out from a folded paper only if it has a line of symmetry.
E has a horizontal line of symmetry. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the E.
N has no line of symmetry. Its two halves never match, so N cannot be cut out by drawing half or a quarter of it.
X has a vertical and a horizontal line. Fold the paper into one-fourth and draw 1/4 of the X.
T has a vertical line. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the T.
K has a horizontal line. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the K.
V has a vertical line. Fold the paper in half and draw 1/2 of the V.
O has a vertical and a horizontal line. Fold the paper into one-fourth and draw 1/4 of the O.
Check: E, X, T, K, V and O have a line of symmetry, and N has none.
items.answer: E, X, T, K, V and O can be cut out: 1/2 for E, T, K and V, and 1/4 for X and O. N cannot be cut out this way.

videos.answer: E, X, T, K, V and O can be cut out: 1/2 for E, T, K and V, and 1/4 for X and O. N cannot be cut out this way.

source: Alphabet Cutout: lines of symmetry in the letters

items.question: Look at the letters E, N, X, T, K, V and O. (a): Which of the letters have a horizontal line of symmetry? ___; (b): Which of the letters have a vertical line of symmetry? ___; (c): Which letters have both vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry? ___
steps: (a): a horizontal line goes across. Fold each letter along a horizontal line: the top half and the bottom half match for E, X, K and O.
(b): a vertical line goes up and down. Fold each letter along a vertical line: the left half and the right half match for X, T, V and O.
(c): the letters in both lists have both lines: X and O.
Check: N is in neither list, because N has no line of symmetry.
items.answer: (a): E, X, K, O; (b): X, T, V, O; (c): X, O

videos.answer: (a): E, X, K, O; (b): X, T, V, O; (c): X, O

source: Let Us Do (cutouts): diya and boat

items.question: Use lines of symmetry to make paper cutouts of diya, boat, and other designs. Look along the border of the page to find the pictures.
steps: Look along the border of the page. The diya and the boat are there, with other pictures such as the heart, the butterfly and the leaf.
The diya has a vertical line of symmetry, down the middle of the flame and the bowl.
Fold a paper in half. Draw half of the diya along the fold, cut along the outline and open the paper: the full diya appears.
The boat also has a vertical line of symmetry, down the middle of the sail and the hull. Fold, draw half of the boat along the fold, cut and open.
Any border picture with a line of symmetry can be cut out in the same way.

source: A paper pinwheel has 4 blades and a dot on the top blade. Tu

items.question: A paper pinwheel has 4 blades and a dot on the top blade. Turn it to the right, the same way each time. Where is the dot after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn and a 3/4 turn?
steps: A full turn is 4 quarter turns, so each quarter turn moves the dot on by one blade.
After a 1/4 turn the dot moves from the top blade to the right blade.
After a second quarter turn the dot is on the bottom blade. Two quarter turns make a 1/2 turn, because 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2.
After a third quarter turn the dot is on the left blade. Three quarter turns make a 3/4 turn.
After the fourth quarter turn the dot is back on the top blade, where it started: a full turn.
Check: 1/4 turn, right blade; 1/2 turn, bottom blade; 3/4 turn, left blade; full turn, top blade.
items.answer: After a 1/4 turn the dot is on the right blade, after a 1/2 turn on the bottom blade, and after a 3/4 turn on the left blade

videos.answer: After a 1/4 turn the dot is on the right blade, after a 1/2 turn on the bottom blade, and after a 3/4 turn on the left blade

source: Does the letter Z have rotational symmetry? Does the letter

items.question: Does the letter Z have rotational symmetry? Does the letter T? Turn each one by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
steps: Z: put a dot on the top left of the Z.
After a 1/4 turn the Z lies on its side and looks like an N, so it does not look the same.
After a 1/2 turn the Z is upside down and looks the same, with the dot now at the bottom right.
After a 3/4 turn the Z lies on its other side and looks like an N again, so it does not look the same.
The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn.

T: after a 1/4 turn the T lies on its side. After a 1/2 turn it is upside down, with the bar at the bottom. After a 3/4 turn it lies on its other side. None of these looks like the T, so the T has no rotational symmetry.
Check: every shape looks the same after a full turn, so the full turn does not count.
items.answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry

videos.answer: The Z has rotational symmetry, at 1/2 turn. The T has no rotational symmetry

source: Let Us Make a Windmill Firki: does it look the same

items.question: Observe the dot in the firki. Does the firki look the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and a full turn? ___
steps: The firki has 4 equal blades. The dot only keeps track of the turn.
After a 1/4 turn each blade has moved to the place of the next blade, so the firki looks the same.
After a 1/2 turn and after a 3/4 turn it looks the same in the same way.
After a full turn the dot is back where it started and the firki looks the same.
So the firki looks the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn. The dot moves, but the firki looks the same.
items.answer: Yes, it looks the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn. The dot moves, but the firki looks the same.

videos.answer: Yes, it looks the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn. The dot moves, but the firki looks the same.

source: Example 1: the letter H turned

items.question: Observe the letter H. Dots have been marked on it to keep track of its orientation. Does the H look the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn? Does it have rotational symmetry? Yes/No.
steps: Turn the H a 1/4 turn: it lies on its side. It does not look the same.
Turn it a 1/2 turn: it is upside down and it looks the same. The dots have moved to the bottom.
Turn it a 3/4 turn: it lies on its other side. It does not look the same.
Turn it a full turn: it is back where it started and looks the same.
The H looks the same after a 1/2 turn, which is smaller than a full turn, so it has rotational symmetry.
items.answer: Yes, at 1/2 turn

videos.answer: Yes, at 1/2 turn

source: Turning Letters: letters I, X and Y

items.question: Observe the letters. Dots have been marked on the letters to keep track of the orientation of letters. You may also cut out the letters and fix the centre point of the letter by a nail or use a tracing paper to check if the letter looks the same when turned. Fill the table for three letters: (a): the letter I, (b): the letter X, (c): the letter Y. For each letter: does it look the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn? Does it have rotational symmetry (Yes/No)?
steps: (a): the I is a straight bar. After a 1/4 turn it lies flat, so it does not look the same. After a 1/2 turn it looks the same. After a 3/4 turn it lies flat again. After a full turn it looks the same. Rotational symmetry: yes, at 1/2 turn.
(b): the X looks the same after a 1/4 turn, after a 1/2 turn, after a 3/4 turn and after a full turn. Rotational symmetry: yes, at 1/4 turn.

(c): the Y lies on its side after a 1/4 turn, is upside down after a 1/2 turn and lies on its other side after a 3/4 turn. None of these looks the same, only the full turn does. Rotational symmetry: no.
Check: only a turn smaller than a full turn counts, so the Y has no rotational symmetry.
items.answer: (a): Yes, at 1/2 turn; (b): Yes, at 1/4 turn; (c): No

videos.answer: (a): Yes, at 1/2 turn; (b): Yes, at 1/4 turn; (c): No

source: Sort the letter M, the letter S and the plus sign into: refl

items.question: Sort the letter M, the letter S and the plus sign into: reflection symmetry only, rotational symmetry only, both symmetries, or neither.
steps: M, Test 1: it has a vertical line of symmetry. Test 2: after a 1/2 turn it looks like a W, so it does not look the same. M has reflection symmetry only.

S, Test 1: fold it along a vertical line or a horizontal line and the halves do not match, so there is no line of symmetry. Test 2: after a 1/2 turn the S looks the same. S has rotational symmetry only.
The plus sign, Test 1: it has a vertical line and a horizontal line. Test 2: it looks the same after a 1/4 turn. It has both symmetries.
Check: each of the three signs went to a different group.
items.answer: M: reflection symmetry only. S: rotational symmetry only. The plus sign: both

videos.answer: M: reflection symmetry only. S: rotational symmetry only. The plus sign: both

source: Let Us Do (digits): symmetry in the digits

items.question: Find symmetry in the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0. (a): Which digit(s) have reflection symmetry? ___; (b): Which digit(s) have rotational symmetry? ___; (c): Which digit(s) have both rotational and reflection symmetries? ___
steps: The digit 1 is drawn as a plain bar, so test the digits as they are drawn in your maths book.
Reflection: fold each digit along a vertical or a horizontal line. 0, 1 and 8 match on both lines, and 3 matches on a horizontal line. 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 match on no line.
Rotation: turn each digit a 1/2 turn. 0, 1 and 8 look the same. A 1/2 turn turns 6 into 9 and 9 into 6, so 6 and 9 do not look the same by themselves. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 do not look the same.
Both: the digits in both lists are 0, 1 and 8.
Check: 3 is in the first list only, and 6 and 9 are in neither list.

source: Let Us Do (digits): the numbers 11 and 1001

items.question: Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11 and 1001. Do these have (a): rotational symmetry, (b): reflection symmetry or (c) both symmetries?
steps: The digit 1 is drawn as a plain bar. Test each number with a fold line and with a 1/2 turn.
11: fold along the vertical line between the two bars and the halves match. Turn it a 1/2 turn: the two bars swap places and the number looks the same.

1001: fold along the vertical line between the two 0s and the halves match. Turn it a 1/2 turn: the first 1 lands at the end, the last 1 lands at the start, and each 0 still looks like a 0, so the number looks the same.
So 11 and 1001 both have reflection symmetry and rotational symmetry.
items.answer: Both numbers have both symmetries: (c)

videos.answer: Both numbers have both symmetries: (c)

source: Let Us Do (digits): examples of 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers

items.question: Give examples of 2-, 3-, and 4-digit numbers which have rotational symmetry, reflection symmetry, or both.
steps: Use the digits you found: 0, 1 and 8 have both symmetries, 3 has a horizontal line only, and 6 and 9 turn into each other after a 1/2 turn.
Rotational symmetry only: 69, 619 and 6969. A 1/2 turn turns 6 into 9 and 9 into 6 and swaps their places, so each number looks the same. None of them has a line of symmetry.
Reflection symmetry only: 38, 383 and 3883. Every digit has a horizontal line of symmetry, so each number has a horizontal line. A 1/2 turn does not keep a 3, so none of them has rotational symmetry.
Both: 88, 808 and 8118. 0, 1 and 8 have a vertical line, and each number reads the same from both ends, so each has a vertical line, and a 1/2 turn keeps each number.
Sample answer: many other numbers work. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer. Rotation only: 69, 619, 6969. Reflection only: 38, 383, 3883. Both: 88, 808, 8118. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer. Rotation only: 69, 619, 6969. Reflection only: 38, 383, 3883. Both: 88, 808, 8118. Your answer may differ.

source: A design has a circle in the middle and one triangle above i

items.question: A design has a circle in the middle and one triangle above it, pointing up. Add triangles so that the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn, and then after a 1/4 turn.
steps: After a 1/2 turn the top triangle lands at the bottom, pointing down. Add a triangle below the circle, pointing down.
Now the design has 1 + 1 = 2 triangles, and it looks the same after a 1/2 turn.
After a 1/4 turn the top triangle lands on the right, pointing right, and the bottom triangle lands on the left, pointing left. Add a triangle on the right and one on the left.
Now the design has 2 + 2 = 4 triangles, one on each side of the circle.
The design looks the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and a full turn: 4 times in a full turn.
Check: after a 1/4 turn each triangle lands on the place of the next triangle.
items.answer: Add a triangle below the circle for a 1/2 turn, then a triangle on the left and on the right for a 1/4 turn

videos.answer: Add a triangle below the circle for a 1/2 turn, then a triangle on the left and on the right for a 1/4 turn

source: A square is cut by its two diagonals into 4 triangles. The t

items.question: A square is cut by its two diagonals into 4 triangles. The top and bottom triangles are orange and the left and right triangles are blue. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn? After a 1/4 turn? Find its lines of symmetry.
steps: Turn it a 1/2 turn: the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, both orange, and the left triangle lands on the right triangle, both blue. It looks the same.
Turn it a 1/4 turn: the top triangle lands on the right triangle, orange on blue. It does not look the same.
Fold along the vertical line: the left triangle lands on the right triangle, blue on blue, and the top and bottom triangles each land on themselves. It is a line of symmetry.
Fold along the horizontal line: the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, orange on orange. It is a line of symmetry.
Fold along a diagonal: the top triangle lands on the left triangle, orange on blue. It is not a line of symmetry.
Check: the design looks the same after a 1/2 turn, not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry.
items.answer: It looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry: the vertical line and the horizontal line

videos.answer: It looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn, and it has 2 lines of symmetry: the vertical line and the horizontal line

source: Making Designs: change the design

items.question: (a): Does the design have rotational symmetry? Yes/No. (b): Try to change the design by adding some shape(s) so that the new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn. Draw the new design in your notebook. (c): Now try to modify or add more shapes so that the new design looks the same after 1/4 turn. Draw the new design in your notebook. (d): Do the new designs have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw the lines of symmetry.
steps: (a): look at the right side. There is a circle at the tip of the right triangle, but nothing at the tip of the left triangle. After a 1/2 turn the circle would land on the left, where there is no circle. So the answer is No.

(b): add a circle at the tip of the left triangle. After a 1/2 turn the top triangle lands on the bottom triangle, the left arm lands on the right arm, and the two circles swap. The new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn.

(c): make all four arms the same. Turn the top and bottom triangles round so that their flat sides touch the middle circle, and put a circle at the tip of each of the four triangles. Every arm is now a triangle with a circle at its tip, so the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn.

(d): the design from (b) has 2 lines of symmetry, a vertical line and a horizontal line through the middle circle. The design from (c) has 4 lines: the vertical line, the horizontal line and the two diagonals.
Sample answer: other changes also work. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: (a): No. (b): add a circle at the left tip. (c): four equal arms with a circle at each tip. (d): yes, 2 lines for (b) and 4 lines for (c). Your drawings may differ.

videos.answer: (a): No. (b): add a circle at the left tip. (c): four equal arms with a circle at each tip. (d): yes, 2 lines for (b) and 4 lines for (c). Your drawings may differ.

source: Let Us Think: the green and pink square

items.question: Look at the design made of 4 squares. Does this design look the same after 1/2 turn? ___ Does the design look the same after 1/4 turn? ___
steps: The design is a square of 4 smaller squares. The top left and the bottom right are green. The top right and the bottom left are pink.
After a 1/2 turn the top left square lands on the bottom right, both green, and the top right square lands on the bottom left, both pink. The design looks the same.
After a 1/4 turn the top left square, green, lands where the top right square is, and that square is pink. The design does not look the same.
Check: the colours decide the answer, so a 1/2 turn works and a 1/4 turn does not.
items.answer: After a 1/2 turn: Yes. After a 1/4 turn: No.

videos.answer: After a 1/2 turn: Yes. After a 1/4 turn: No.

source: Let Us Think: colour the square

items.question: Colour the square given in the figure using two colours so that the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn. How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?
steps: The dashed lines cut the square into 8 equal triangles round the middle.
A 1/4 turn moves every triangle on by 2 places.
So colour the triangles one after the other in two colours, orange, blue, orange, blue, and so on all the way round.
Now each triangle lands on a triangle of its own colour after a 1/4 turn.
The design looks the same after a 1/4 turn, a 1/2 turn, a 3/4 turn and the full turn: 4 times in a full turn.
Check: 8 triangles ÷ 2 places = 4 quarter turns make a full turn.
items.answer: Colour the 8 triangles in two colours, one after the other. The shape looks the same 4 times in a full turn.

videos.answer: Colour the 8 triangles in two colours, one after the other. The shape looks the same 4 times in a full turn.

source: Let Us Think: reflection symmetry in the designs

items.question: Do these designs have reflection symmetry also? Draw the line(s) of symmetry.
steps: The two designs are the green and pink square and the square coloured orange and blue.
Green and pink square: fold it along a diagonal, from one corner to the opposite corner. The two halves land on each other, green on green and pink on pink. So each diagonal is a line of symmetry.
Fold it along the vertical line: the green square would land on a pink square. That is not a line of symmetry. The horizontal line does the same.
So the green and pink square has 2 lines of symmetry, the two diagonals.
Orange and blue square: fold it along any dashed line. Every triangle would land on a triangle of the other colour. So there is no line of symmetry.
This design looks the same after a turn, but it has no reflection symmetry.
items.answer: Green and pink square: yes, 2 lines (the two diagonals). Orange and blue square: no line of symmetry.

videos.answer: Green and pink square: yes, 2 lines (the two diagonals). Orange and blue square: no line of symmetry.

source: Let Us Do (squares and triangles): make designs

items.question: Cut out squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length. These are provided at the end of the book. Make different symmetrical designs by using these two shapes.
steps: Take squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length.
Place a square in the middle and a triangle on each of its 4 sides, with a side of the triangle along a side of the square. The design looks the same after every 1/4 turn and has 4 lines of symmetry.
Place one triangle on top of one square: a house shape. It has 1 vertical line of symmetry and no turn that makes it look the same.
Place 4 triangles in a row, one pointing up, then one pointing down, and so on. This slanted strip looks the same after a 1/2 turn and has no line of symmetry.
Sample answer: many other designs work. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer: a square with a triangle on each side, a house shape, a slanted strip of 4 triangles. Your designs may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: a square with a triangle on each side, a house shape, a slanted strip of 4 triangles. Your designs may differ.

source: Let Us Do (squares and triangles): the shape with four squares

items.question: Does this shape have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw its line(s) of symmetry. Does it have rotational symmetry? If yes, at which turn? Does it have both symmetries?
steps: The shape has 4 squares in 2 rows of 2, and 4 triangles: one at the left end and one at the right end of each row.
Vertical line: fold down the middle, between the two columns of squares. The left triangles land on the right triangles and the left squares on the right squares. It is a line of symmetry.
Horizontal line: fold along the line between the two rows. The top row lands on the bottom row. It is a second line of symmetry.
Turn: after a 1/4 turn the triangles would land above and below the squares, where there are none, so it does not look the same.
After a 1/2 turn each triangle lands on the triangle at the other end and each square lands on the square opposite to it, so it looks the same. It has rotational symmetry at 1/2 turn.
So the shape has both symmetries.
items.answer: Reflection symmetry: yes, 2 lines (one vertical, one horizontal). Rotational symmetry: yes, at 1/2 turn. Both: yes.

videos.answer: Reflection symmetry: yes, 2 lines (one vertical, one horizontal). Rotational symmetry: yes, at 1/2 turn. Both: yes.

source: Let Us Do (squares and triangles): sort your designs

items.question: Now, make your designs. Sort your designs in 3 categories: designs with only rotational symmetry, designs with only reflection symmetry, and designs with both rotational and reflection symmetry.
steps: Test each design twice: fold it along lines for reflection symmetry, and turn it a 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 turn for rotational symmetry.
Only rotational symmetry: the slanted strip of 4 triangles. It looks the same after a 1/2 turn and has no line of symmetry.
Only reflection symmetry: the house shape, a triangle on top of a square. It has 1 vertical line and no turn that works.
Both: a square with a triangle on each side. It has 4 lines and looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
Sample answer: your designs may be different. Your answer may differ.

source: A block is carved in the shape of a leaf with a stem down th

items.question: A block is carved in the shape of a leaf with a stem down the middle. Its half print shows only the left half of the leaf. What does the whole print look like?
steps: The half print has one straight edge. That edge is the line of symmetry.
The straight edge runs down the middle of the leaf, along the stem.
Draw the same half on the other side of the line, as if the paper were folded along the edge.
The two halves together make the whole leaf.
Check: fold the whole print along the line and the two halves land on each other.
items.answer: The whole print is the half print together with its copy on the other side of the straight edge

videos.answer: The whole print is the half print together with its copy on the other side of the straight edge

source: A flower block is stamped 2 times, with a 1/2 turn between t

items.question: A flower block is stamped 2 times, with a 1/2 turn between the stamps. Does the print look the same after a 1/2 turn? After a 1/4 turn?
steps: The first stamp puts a flower at the top.
A 1/2 turn of the block puts the second flower at the bottom.
Turn the print a 1/2 turn: the top flower lands at the bottom and the bottom flower lands at the top. The print looks the same.
Turn the print a 1/4 turn: the flowers would land at the sides, where there are none. The print does not look the same.
Check: 2 stamps match after a 1/2 turn only.
items.answer: After a 1/2 turn it looks the same, and after a 1/4 turn it does not

videos.answer: After a 1/2 turn it looks the same, and after a 1/4 turn it does not

source: Block Printing: design B

items.question: The design B looks the same after every ___ turn. This design has ___ symmetry.
steps: The design B is made of 4 hearts placed round the middle.
Turn it a 1/4 turn: the top heart lands where the right heart is, the right heart where the bottom heart is, and so on. The design looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
The dashed vertical line and the dashed horizontal line are lines of symmetry: the left half matches the right half, and the top half matches the bottom half.
So the design has rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry.
Check: it looks the same after a turn and it has lines of symmetry, so it has both.
items.answer: Every 1/4 turn. It has both rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry.

videos.answer: Every 1/4 turn. It has both rotational symmetry and reflection symmetry.

source: Let Us Do (border shapes): reflection and rotational symmetry

items.question: Observe the shapes given on the border. Which of the shapes have reflection symmetry? Put a tick mark on them. Put a star mark on the shapes that have rotational symmetry.
steps: Test each shape with a fold line (reflection symmetry) and with a turn (rotational symmetry). The shapes are numbered 1 to 19 round the border from the top-left corner, going to the right, then down, then to the left, then up.
Shape 1, three pink triangles touching at their corners: 3 lines of symmetry, and it looks the same after a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 2, the green six-pointed star: 6 lines, and it looks the same after a 1/6 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 3, the yellow six-sided shape: 2 lines, a vertical and a horizontal one, and it looks the same after a 1/2 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 4, three lilac circles joined to the middle, drawn nearly even: 3 lines, and a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 5, the green triangle with grey corners: 3 lines, and a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 6, the pink rectangle: 2 lines, and a 1/2 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 7, the grey diamond: 2 lines, and a 1/2 turn. Tick and star.

Shape 12, the pink triangle with three teal circles: 3 lines, and a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 13, the orange slanted four-sided shape: no line of symmetry, but it looks the same after a 1/2 turn. Star only.
Shape 14, the yellow triangle with three small grey triangles: 3 lines, and a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 15, the thin pink triangle with a square corner: no line of symmetry and no turn that works. No mark.
Shape 16, the two maroon triangles touching at their points: 2 lines, and a 1/2 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 17, the circle: every line through the middle is a line of symmetry, and it looks the same after every turn. Tick and star.
Shape 18, the blue square: 4 lines, and a 1/4 turn. Tick and star.
Shape 19, the purple triangle with three equal sides: 3 lines, and a 1/3 turn. Tick and star.
Check: 17 shapes get a tick mark, all except 13 and 15, and 18 shapes get a star mark, all except 15. 17 + 2 = 19 and 18 + 1 = 19.

source: Project Work: vegetable blocks

items.question: Create symmetrical patterns and designs using vegetable blocks. Some are shown below.
steps: Cut a vegetable, such as a potato, to get a flat face, and carve a simple shape on it. A ladyfinger cut across also gives a flower-like face.
Dip the flat face in colour and press it on paper to make a print.
For a design that looks the same after every 1/4 turn, stamp the block, turn the paper a 1/4 turn, and stamp again, 4 times in all.
For a design with a line of symmetry, use a block that has its own line of symmetry and stamp it on the two sides of a line drawn on the paper, the same distance from the line.
Sort your prints: only rotational symmetry, only reflection symmetry, or both.
Sample answer: your patterns may be different. Your answer may differ.
